<reason>CON won by turning urgency into effectiveness: rates restrain demand but do not build homes, can hurt incomes and construction, while slowing inflation does not reverse levels. A's pressure forced PRO to concede prices can rebound and to demand tightening even at target with scarcity rents, which A framed as sectoral overreach that sacrifices paychecks without delivering usable relief.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's permanence attack - slowing increases is not reversing levels and rebound after rate cuts erases lasting benefit - answered by B's concession in A2 that no policy freezes prices, which A then used to collapse PRO's temporary-pain vs permanent-gain asymmetry.</best_rebuttal>
